gaps: The graphic sources conflict: the Academia Sinica evolution page interprets the seal-script graph as 人+至 with 人 transformed/reinterpreted as 刀, while Shuowen and other databases analyze it as 至+刀. The actual transition, its chronology, and whether any form involves corruption are not established by the inspected text sources.

The inspected Taiwan MOE entry marks its paleographic reference collections unavailable. The claim that 到 is absent from oracle-bone records or first appears in a particular bronze inscription is not established here; a captions-only database lists bronze specimens but the glyph images were not inspected.

Received poem and Analects examples attest 到 with arrival/reach or temporal extension senses, but source access and dating limitations mean exact first attestation dates and chronological semantic development remain unresolved. No gloss-list order was used to infer chronology.

The phonetic relationship 刀~到 is supported by same-system historical reconstruction comparisons and the Shuowen phonetic account. The disputed ultimate etymology of the spoken word 刀 is a separate lexical question; no borrowing of the whole graph 到 is proposed, and no claim about an unrecoverable depicted object’s name is needed for the phonetic-component analysis.

No independently verified account was found for how the later senses ‘thorough/careful’, ‘deceive’, or ‘say/state’ developed from the arrival/reach sense; the CUHK dictionary gives citations but not the semantic links.

Searches for the actual Analects and Ctext dictionary pages encountered HTTP 403; the search-result snippets were recorded only as such and should be verified from an accessible critical edition if exact textual witnesses are required.

The seal-form account from Academia Sinica (人 + 至, with 人 reinterpreted as phonetic 刀) conflicts with the standard 至 + 刀 analysis reported by Shuowen and several databases. The actual graphic transition, chronology, and possibility of graphic corruption remain unresolved.

No inspected primary image or accessible paleographic catalog established an oracle-bone form or the earliest securely dated inscription of 到. Database labels identify bronze examples, but the image content was not inspected in this research stage.

The received 詩經·韓奕 phrase is cited as an early textual use, but its composition and transmission dates are not established by the inspected sources. The Analects citation and its precise textual witness were not reverified in this stage.

The dictionary’s additional senses ‘go’, ‘thorough/careful’, ‘deceive’, and ‘say/state’ have cited examples, but their respective dates and semantic pathways are not adequately established by the inspected sources. The independent linguistic study does describe later constructional developments for 到 as a verb and complement.

刀~到 phonetic correspondence is independently supported within the Baxter–Sagart reconstruction system, and 至 is identified as semantic in multiple dictionary accounts. 刀’s pictorial/object referent and the ultimate etymology or original pronunciation of the spoken word 刀 do not establish the phonetic role and are not needed for this compound analysis.

Commons returned search descriptions for 到 historical-style files, but relevant image description pages failed to open. File-specific direct image URLs and reuse rights were not verified; no image is included.

The exact 到-seal.svg Commons page and upload.wikimedia.org SVG both returned cache-miss errors; the exact Commons imageinfo API lookup was inaccessible, and the Wikibooks file page also failed. The supplied local copy was not downloaded or pixel-inspected here. Its literal identity, provenance, script-period basis, and reuse rights therefore remain unverified, so it cannot be selected.

The local Unihan kMandarin rows were checked, but the required official Unicode Unihan records for 刀, 到, and 至 could not be opened. Their local readings are not externally verified click-through evidence in this result.

Baxter–Sagart local rows were checked for all three characters, but the character-specific entries were not read from the authors’ external PDF during this invocation. The authors’ project page verifies the dataset’s provenance and system context, not those individual forms.

The sources support both the Shuowen-style 至+刀 analysis and Academia Sinica’s account of 人+至 developing into a phonosemantic graph. The precise graphic transition and chronology, and whether any corruption occurred, remain unresolved.
